why: Permit decides, forbid explains: one @tier permit per tier carries the decision and an empty policy set denies, so the loader's completeness check guards the explanation rather than the decision. `ids` are the same ids guidance.json renders and the Rego and CEL twins report; the loader must find one @id forbid per id, one @assembly forbid per tier, and one @tier permit per tier. The forbids are guarded `context has probe` and the permit `!(context has probe)`; the proxy checks those guards on every call.
